title: DECISION: Write-before-ioctl for KEY_IMPORT avoids large stack frames
description: KEY_IMPORT receives raw key bytes via write(2) (accumulated in inbuf), not embedded in the ioctl struct. The ioctl struct carries only metadata. Embedding key bytes would require an 8192-byte struct on the kernel stack for every call (worst case: ML-DSA-87 at 4896 bytes + headroom). The kernel has a ~1 KB stack frame guideline; a 8 KB ioctl struct violates it and causes stack overflow on PQ key imports. The write-before-ioctl pattern heap-allocates exactly what the key requires, then zeroizes and frees. If a future PQ key exceeds CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_IMPORT_MAXLEN, raise the constant — do not change the pattern.
